{{Quote|By bringing the entire galaxy under one law, one language, and the enlightened guidance of one individual, the corruption that plagued the Republic in its later years will never take root.|Palpatine|<ref name="Inaugural Edition">{{InsiderCite|84|Republic HoloNet News Special Inaugural Edition 16:5:241}}</ref>}}
'''Galactic Emperor''',<ref name="IGP">[[Intergalactic Passport (real-life artifact)|Intergalactic Passport]]</ref> sometimes referred to as '''Grand Emperor'''<ref name="Kenner">{{KennerCite|set=Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (toy line)|pack=Dagobah Action Playset|altlink=http://theswca.com/index.php?action=disp_item&item_id=39653}}</ref> or simply as the '''Emperor''', was the [[King/Legends|sovereign ruler]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and, [[Fel Empire|later]], under the [[Fel dynasty]]. The position and title was first formed, alongside the Galactic Empire itself, in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] during [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] [[Declaration of a New Order]] immediately after the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. The female holder of this position, at least [[post-Imperial era]], is generally referred to as '''Empress'''. The office was often referred to abstractly as the '''Imperial Executive''' or the '''Imperial throne'''.

==Powers and functions==
===Governance===
{{Quote|As the Emperor wills it, so shall it be.|Darth Vader|<ref name="A New Hope novel">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novelization]]</ref>}}
The Galactic Emperor's power and authority were mainly derived from those of the [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] and the additional rights, responsibilities, and powers bestowed upon that office by the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Senate]] during the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]] and [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. It also derived power (at least nominally) from the Senate itself. The Emperor was the ultimate head of the [[Imperial Ruling Council/Legends|Imperial Ruling Council]], and was, at least nominally or symbolically, advised by the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]]. Officially, the Galactic Emperor does not directly interfere with local politics. During the reign of [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], the Emperor was effectively an absolute monarch.<ref name="Dark Times 1">[[Dark Times 1|''Dark Times'' 1]]</ref>

[[File:Emperor_Palpatine_AoN.png|thumb|left|180px|Emperor Palpatine on his throne]]
The Emperor was the [[Head of State/Legends|Head of State]], Head of Government, and the [[Commander-in-Chief/Legends|Commander-in-Chief]] of the Galactic Empire, and had absolute authority over the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]], the bureaucracy, and the entire Empire and sectors itself. The Emperor had sole power to appoint, dismiss, approve, and supervise the [[Moff/Legends|regional governors]]. The Emperor organized and declared the budget, economy, taxes, and trade, ordered the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]] into session, dismissed it from meeting at will, declared its agenda, and proposed, rejected, and initiated all Senatorial bills. The Emperor also controlled, supervised, and disbanded the Courts and had the final judicial say. As such, the Emperor's mere word was enough for the Imperial hierarchy to enact his will.<ref name="A New Hope novel" /> Those members of the Imperial government that saw particular favor with the Galactic Emperor often saw themselves elevated to positions of significant galactic power. Largely due to Palpatine's usage of these promotions, those within his inner circle formed a society composed of twisted sycophants and back-stabbers.<ref name="Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> In addition, he also issued via the Imperial Senate [[Intergalactic Passport]]s to allow their bearers access to various planets controlled by the Empire, as well as the six primary galaxies.<ref name="IGP" />

As Emperor, Palpatine retained the emergency powers that had been voted to him during the Clone Wars, allowing him to rule under what amounted to martial law. He could execute, imprison, exile, banish, or confiscate anyone or anything solely on his authority. The Emperor could also issue executive orders, and proclamations with the legal force of law in the Empire, even more powerful than those issued by the Senate. The Emperor supervised, directed, appointed, and dismissed all officials in the government, and created, disbanded, supervised, and directed all governmental administrations, agencies, commissions, and boards. He could also confiscate all assets from defeated worlds at his order, something most especially seen in the first year of the Galactic Empire's formation.<ref name="Dark Times 1" /> He can also redirect funds from various departments for weapons development, even when such actions are illegal.<ref name="DSOTM">''[[Death Star Owner's Technical Manual]]''</ref><ref name="The Far Orbit Project">{{WEGCite|story=The Capture of Coh Veshiv|book=The Far Orbit Project}}</ref>

In addition to processing judgment to criminals via the Judiciary system, the Emperor, should the charge be serious enough, such as [[Treason/Legends|high treason]],<ref name="SW:EAW">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]''</ref> can also personally deliver the sentenced punishment to the criminal in question.<ref name="Battle for the Sunstar">{{Ewoks|Battle for the Sunstar}}</ref> The Emperor can also preside over the [[Shaldania Parade]] from the Palatial Balcony, as well as observe and direct the public executions of "Enemies of the Empire" during [[Carnival Week]] and [[New Year Fete Week/Legends|New Year Fete Week]], the latter of which the Emperor also has the authority to force in the execution proceedings during the festivities.

Regarding marriages to the Galactic Emperor, the legal details of a potential Emperor's wedding were specifically included in Imperial law, and in fact specified that the bride would forfeit her rights and become the groom's property&mdash;although that particular law may have been a [[Church of the Dark Side]] fabrication.<ref name="Queen">''[[Queen of the Empire]]''</ref>

===Military===
In addition to his virtually absolute actions within the governance within the Empire, he also had near-total control within the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]], with effective authority resting in the hands of the secondary-ranking [[Supreme Commander (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Supreme Commander]]. The Emperor is the one who gives orders to at the very least the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]], which are transmitted from [[Army Command]] down via a hierarchy.<ref name="Imperial Handbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref> The development of superweapons under the Emperor's reign often necessitated that he visit the site development to personally inspect the development, evidenced by Palpatine's visitation of both Death Stars.<ref name="Betrayal">''[[Star Wars: Empire: Betrayal]]''</ref><ref name="ROJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> As such, while the first Death Star was run by a triumvirate composed of [[Battle Station Command/Legends|Battle Station Command]], [[Naval Command (Imperial)|Naval Command]], and Army Command, the Emperor superceded their authority when he made direct visits to the battle station, and also supplied inputs to the development of the station, including adding in a contingency plan to make either [[Emperor's throne room (Death Star)/Legends|the tower]] [[Emperor's Throne Room/Legends|throne room]] or one of the lesser sections assume command if the [[Overbridge (Death Star I)/Legends|Overbridge]] was irreparably damaged. He also can give inputs to the designs of various weaponry, as evidenced by his personally suggesting that the superdreadnought ''[[Eye of Palpatine]]'' specifically resemble an asteroid complete with impact craters, insisting it was necessary camouflage for baffling scanners.<ref name="DSOTM" /> In addition, the Emperor alongside [[Imperial High Command/Legends|Imperial High Command]] were the ones who gave explicit authorization of using the Death Star's superlaser, even against targeted worlds, with any unauthorized usage of the superlaser being forbidden, and the Emperor is also the one to provide current codes for firing the superlaser.<ref name="Imperial Handbook" /> He can also place various weapons and vehicles into lockdown should there be a grave security risk with them, as evidenced by his suspending the [[Missile Boat]]'s deployment due to then-[[Zaarin insurrection|current]] [[Sealion|events]].<ref name="TIE Fighter">[[Star Wars: TIE Fighter (video game)|''Star Wars: TIE Fighter'']]</ref> He can also oversee the development of new weapons and training new personnel besides superweapons should they be deemed important enough, such as his personally observing the development of the [[Cuis clone]]s,<ref name="A Two-Edged Sword">{{InsiderCite|85|A Two-Edged Sword}}</ref> as well as his observance of the final test to become members of his royal guard.<ref name="Crimson Empire">[[Star Wars: Crimson Empire (series)|''Star Wars: Crimson Empire'' series]]</ref><ref name="Imperial Handbook" /> The Emperor could also personally lead the military forces into direct warfare should the battle or even military operation be important enough to require his presence,<ref name="ROJ" /><ref name="DE">''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire]]''</ref> even operating his own [[Emperor's fleet|personal fleet]] of starships for the occasion.<ref name="The Force Unleashed">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref> The Emperor can also redirect virtually the entire [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] (and possibly the entire Imperial Military) back to Coruscant when giving a speech to his military and citizens, having done so [[State of the Galactic Civil War|once]] in 3 ABY. The Emperor can also attend and present starfighter squadrons, such as the 181st Imperial Fighter Wing, should they be exceptionally renowned and skilled during ceremonies.<ref name="Author's Cut 10">[[Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut]] ([http://www.starwars.com/news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-10-the-rise-of-the-empire Part 10: The Rise of the Empire])</ref> The Emperor can even, should the actions of one of his soldiers be extraordinary enough, personally award medals, including the coveted [[Emperor's Will (medal)/Legends|Emperor's Will]], to the recipient at his palace.<ref name="TIE Fighter" /> The Emperor also has the power to promote Grand Admirals and Grand Moffs. Likewise, the Emperor can also redirect segments of the military, such as the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]], to other sectors, whether it be for a conflict or to sell people into the slave market.<ref name="Dark Times 2">[[Dark Times 2|''Dark Times'' 2]]</ref> In addition, if the Emperor demands to make contact with one of his officers, even in the middle of a military operation, the officer is obliged to temporarily disengage from his current assignment, even physically relocate if they were currently in a difficult environment to ensure a clear transmission. This was made especially apparent in the aftermath of the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], where [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], who at the time was having [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]] hunt down the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] in the [[Hoth asteroid field/Legends|Hoth asteroid field]], ordered for the [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']] to move out of the asteroid field after learning that Palpatine had demanded for Vader to contact him.<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref> He can also order purges within his own military, especially if some officers were showing signs of anti-Imperial sentiments.<ref name="Dark Times 1" />

[[File:Arrival-ROTJHD.png|thumb|right|260px|One of the Emperor's arrival ceremonies.]]

Whenever the Emperor arrived on a military installation, he was frequently met with an air parade of Imperial starfighter wings, especially TIE fighters, and also had thousands of massed troops, including Stormtroopers, and technicians standing at attention.<ref name="ROJ" /><ref name="Visual Dictionary" /> The Emperor's Royal Guard often preceded out before the Emperor. In addition, his shuttle is often escorted by some squadrons of TIE fighters, including the [[The Emperor's Sword|Emperor's Sword]] and [[Emperor's Shield]] squadrons. Although Emperor Palpatine acted as the Commander-in-Chief of the Imperial Military, he rarely left his palace on Coruscant, which resulted in relatively few Imperial personnel ever actually seeing their leader.<ref name="Complete Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

==Succession==
{{Quote|You [Sith spirits] are long dead... But it is I who rule the galaxy... Forever!|Palpatine, in what is ultimately his final trek to Onderon|<ref name="EE2" />}}
[[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] was the first and only official [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] of the first Galactic Empire&mdash;most of the Imperial leaders who followed were not recognized by all Imperials or never made use of the title of Emperor. One, [[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]], seems to have legitimately held the title in the interim between Palpatine's death at [[Endor/Legends|Endor]] and his expected return. Pestage was possibly killed before Palpatine did return, leaving the throne apparently unoccupied.<ref name="Rebellion Era Sourcebook">''[[Rebellion Era Sourcebook]]''</ref><ref name="Omnibus: X-wing Rogue Squadron Volume 3">''[[Star Wars Omnibus: X-Wing Rogue Squadron Volume 3]]''</ref> In addition, the supposed son of Emperor Palpatine, [[Trioculus]], had been [[Kessendra Coronation|crowned]], although it was left disputed as to whether it was valid.<ref name="The Glove of Darth Vader">''[[The Glove of Darth Vader]]''</ref>

Emperor Palpatine's official heir would normally be Lord Darth Vader, as he was his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] and the Supreme Commander of the Imperial Forces. Though initially he intended the latter to surpass him and follow in his footsteps<ref name="Revenge of the Sith">{{Film|III}}</ref>, there were indications that the [[Duel on Mustafar/Legends|incident]] on [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]] ultimately abolished this desire and he no longer deemed his right-hand a worthy legacy &mdash; Palpatine eventually wanted Vader's secret apprentice [[Galen Marek]],<ref name="The Force Unleashed" /> and later Vader's son, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], to slay the cyborg and assume his place at the side of the Emperor.<ref name="ROJ" /> However, Palpatine had also prepared [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] bodies of himself to take his seat after his death, reducing the likelihood of needing a real heir even further.<ref name="DE" /><ref name="Dark Empire II">''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire II]]''</ref> In addition, he also stated prior to his final death to various Sith spirits that he intended to rule the galaxy for all eternity,<ref name="EE2" /> making it very unlikely that he ever truly intended to have a line of succession if it could be avoided. Despite this, however, Palpatine nonetheless arranged for the Dark Empire to be run on autopilot in the event that he ended up killed before he could utilize soul transference.<ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

In the [[Declaration of a New Order]], Palpatine's speech had indicated that the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]] would elect the Galactic Emperor, but no one in the Imperial High Command had any desire to restore a body that would probably dissolve the Empire, so many Imperial [[Commander/Legends|commanders]] became rogue [[Warlord/Legends|warlords]] after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]].

There were also attempts to have successions via lineage, which either involved blood lineage from remote relatives (such as [[Ederlathh Pallopides/Legends|Ederlathh Pallopides]], the great-niece of Palpatine),<ref name="DES">''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref> or from people rumored to have been sired by Palpatine himself (such as [[Irek Ismaren]]). Most of the latter instances were done to act as power-brokers.<ref name="CotJ">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']]</ref>

After the final death of Palpatine in [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]], [[Xandel Carivus]] proclaimed himself the Emperor, but was soon killed by [[Kir Kanos]].

Under the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]], the role of Imperial Head of State was assumed by Supreme Commander of the Imperial Fleet.

It was unclear what led to the appointment of [[Jagged Fel]] as Emperor, but the title became a hereditary one, passed on among members of the [[Fel dynasty]] such as [[Roan Fel]], though the Emperor shared power with a [[Council of Moffs/Legends|Council of Moffs]] rather than holding absolute authority. In addition, the Emperor was also constantly at the mercy of the [[Imperial Knight]]s, where the Emperor will be summarily executed if the Emperor started showing signs of adopting Dark Side behavior and was unwilling to go back from the Dark Side. This policy was implemented in order to ensure they not have a repeat of Palpatine's actions during his rule of the first Galactic Empire.

When the [[One Sith]] took over, [[Darth Krayt]] abolished the hereditary system and claimed the title of Galactic Emperor for his version of the [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Galactic Empire]]. [[Roan Fel]] still claimed the title from his [[Empire-in-exile]] during the [[Second Imperial Civil War]], and upon the conclusion of the war the deaths of both Krayt and Roan Fel resulted in Princess [[Marasiah Fel]] rising to become Empress of a now reunited Empire.

==Style of office==
{{Quote|Your Majesty, it has long been my contention that your New Order needs one undeniable and overwhelming symbol to impress and, yes, frighten the masses.|Moff Tarkin, in a private message to Emperor Palpatine|<ref name="ISB">''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Dodonnautem.jpg|thumb|left|250px|"His Excellency, Emperor Palpatine", one of the addresses for the Galactic Emperor]]
Under the rule of Palpatine, the Galactic Emperor was formally referred to as "His Imperial Majesty, Emperor Palpatine"<ref name="ISB" /> (as well as simply "His Imperial Majesty"<ref name="Imperial Handbook" />) or "His Excellency, Emperor Palpatine."<ref name="Loyalties">[[Republic 78|''Republic'' 78]]</ref> Both "Your Majesty,"<ref name="Revenge of the Sith">{{Film|III}}</ref> and "Your Highness" were accepted forms of oral address.<ref name="ROJ" /><ref name="The Force Unleashed" /> Governor [[Wilek Nereus]] was known to refer to the Emperor as his "Most Excellent Imperial Master Palpatine" in his messages. While Nereus used the third person in direct address as a mark of courtesy,<ref name="TTB">''[[The Truce at Bakura]]''</ref> [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]] did not.<ref name="ISB" /> At any rate, Palpatine was usually referred to as just "[[the Emperor]]" in the context of non-official, everyday conversations, even between military officers.<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> The official title of "The Galactic Emperor" was also enclosed in the official statements included in issued Intergalactic Passports.<ref name="IGP" /> At least one other official title was "Grand Emperor."<ref name="Kenner" />

Certain individuals had their own, non-official way to address their Imperial sovereign. Despite being part of the Imperial hierarchy by the Empire's late reign, Darth Vader always addressed the Emperor as "my master," when meeting with him in person, a sign of their mentor&ndash;disciple relation in the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark arts]] of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].<ref name="ROJ" /> Vader would also use the pronoun "thy" instead of the more common "your," when asking what the Emperor's bidding was.<ref name="ESB" /><ref name="ROJ" /> [[Prince/Legends|Prince]] [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor]], a [[Falleen/Legends|Falleen]] [[Noble/Legends|noble]] and the leader of the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] criminal organization, addressed Palpatine as "my Emperor."<ref name="SOTE">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' novel]]</ref> [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], an enemy of the Empire, when encountering Palpatine in his senate rotunda chamber, sarcastically referred to Palpatine as simply "Emperor."<ref name="Revenge of the Sith" /> Luke Skywalker, a member of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] and fledgling [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]], when rejecting Palpatine's request for him to induct himself into the Sith as his apprentice shortly after Luke defeated Vader, referred to Palpatine as "Your Highness,"<ref name="ROJ" /> with [[Galen Marek]] at one point referring to Palpatine by that title under similar circumstances during their duel.<ref name="The Force Unleashed" /> Finally, those who knew that Palpatine was a [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] usually called him "my Lord," as did [[Jeng Droga]],<ref name="tkc">{{JournalCite|7|The Kaal Connection}}</ref> one of the [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hands]].<ref name="JvS">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> The Sith spirits on Korriban, when addressing Palpatine when he entered the Tomb of Darth Vader, also referred to him as the "Emperor of numberless worlds."<ref name="EE2">[[Empire's End 2|''Empire's End'' 2]]</ref>

By the time of Operation Shadow Hand, Palpatine was also given the title of "His Immortal Majesty," in reference to his revival from his death at Endor via [[essence transfer]].<ref name="TTSP">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/source/praji/20090205.html|text=Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji|int=Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji}}</ref> Although not an official title of office, Palpatine after his revival also adopted the title of [[Omnipotent Battle Leader]], which he used to sway several feuding [[Warlord/Legends|warlords]] into joining him before officially unveiling his revival.<ref name="Imperial Warlords">{{SW|url=news/the-imperial-warlords-despoilers-of-an-empire-part-1|series=The Imperial Warlords: Despoilers of an Empire|text=Part 1|nolive=1}}</ref>

During the time of the Fel Empire, the reigning Emperor (or Empress) is often addressed as "His Imperial Majesty," or in the case of the Empress, "Her Imperial Majesty," with it also being used for any ships belonging to the Empire.<ref name="Legacy 2, Issue 6">[[Legacy (2013) 6|''Legacy'' (2013) 6]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The title of Galactic Emperor was first mentioned &mdash; although without the 'Galactic' adjective &mdash; in the [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]] of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']], ghostwritten by [[Alan Dean Foster]] and published in [[1976]]. The full title was first used with the [[Intergalactic Passport (real-life artifact)|Intergalactic Passport]] backstage pass for filming of [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']].

In the JC Penny catalogue description for the ''Darth Vader Star Destroyer'' playset, the portrait of the Grand Vizier was misidentified as "Grand Emperor".<ref name="SWCA">{{WebCite|url=http://theswca.com/images-toys/figuretoys/dvsd.html|text=Darth Vader's Star Destroyer Action Playset|work=theswca|archivedate=20201224223722}}</ref>

[[Kyle Katarn]] becomes the new Emperor in the alternative non-[[canon]] option of ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II]]'', succeeding [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]]. Similarly, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], under the influence of the [[Son/Legends|Son]], became both the founder and Emperor of the Galactic Empire upon defeating both Yoda and Sidious when the latter two teamed up in the Infinities comic "Clone Wars: Infinities: What if the Father never rescued Anakin from the Dark Side?" in ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Magazine 7]]''. The Dark Side ending of the ''Revenge of the Sith'' video game has Vader effectively assuming command of the Empire after Sidious, having already become Emperor, gave him his new lightsaber and using it to skewer his master before the latter could react.

There is some confusion as to whether [[Ysanne Isard]] actually claimed the title Empress or not. While ''[[Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties]]'' referred to her as Empress, other works such as ''[[X-Wing: Wedge's Gamble]]'' contradict this (indeed, she claims it would be premature to name an Emperor while the New Republic still exists), and it is possible that this reference was figurative.

In the novelization of ''A New Hope'', Obi-Wan mentions that there have been multiple emperors, with only the later ones becoming corrupt. It also establishes that the man once called Senator Palpatine was a mere puppet dictator.<ref name="A New Hope novel" /> This was inspired by the [[The Star Wars rough draft|rough draft]] of the script for the film, where there had never been a Republic, only an originally-benign Empire which fell to evil.<ref name="Rough Draft">{{WebCite|url=https://www.starwarz.com/starkiller/the-star-wars-rough-draft|text=''The Star Wars: Rough Draft''|work=[https://www.starwarz.com/starkiller Starkiller — The Jedi Bendu Script Site]|archivedate=20240601042406}}</ref>
There was originally going to be a plot point involving the successor to the title of Galactic Emperor in the game ''[[The New Emperor]]''. However, this plot development was cut when the game itself ended up cancelled. Similarly, concept art for what was going to be ''Star Wars: Battlefront IV'' revealed that one what-if concept involved Darth Vader becoming the Galactic Emperor, with his possessing at least two variants of his armor.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2018-03-13-cancelled-star-wars-battlefield-4-art-shows-dark-side-luke-jedi-maul|text=Cancelled Star Wars Battlefront 4 art shows dark side Luke, Jedi Maul|author=Philips, Tom|date=2018-04-11|archivedate=20200510180856}}</ref>
